concepts.definition: F15 is the release and successor-conservation family. Its instance premises are recursive products, published cuts, mutable carriers, derived assets, external services and successor lines. It traces, but does not own, FOUNDATIONS §2 lineage objects. Its table distinguishes commitment-derived consequences from domain and policy choices and their owners.

grounding.quote: Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are

concepts.label: Release and successor conservation

concepts.definition: The lineage taxonomy distinguishes substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition. A mutable source workspace lacks fixed product identity. An install used as builder substrate binds as a development product without transferring meaning or authority to the authored product. Product definition is a source-project surface rather than the released artifact.

grounding.quote: substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition are distinct objects.

concepts.label: Product lineage objects

concepts.definition: A stable repository-local key assigned by the Product release authority to one independently released source project.
concepts.label: Project Release Namespace

concepts.definition: The exact repository-relative source-project root and Git tree object selected for one cut.

grounding.quote:
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;

concepts.label: Project Subtree

concepts.definition: The mutable source-project state constructing a possible successor; a realisation of FOUNDATIONS §2 Candidate Source.

grounding.quote:
- Candidate Source: the candidate source of FOUNDATIONS §2, the mutable
  source-project state constructing a possible successor;

concepts.label: Candidate Source

concepts.definition: A mutable project-qualified carrier for the current candidate window.

grounding.quote:
- RC Branch: a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current
  candidate window;

concepts.label: RC Branch

concepts.definition: An annotated project-qualified Git tag together with its exact Product release subject, identifying one published candidate and, once accepted, one released Product. It realises the release cut.
concepts.label: Immutable RC Cut

concepts.definition: A mutable project-qualified tag alias naming the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for one project and version line. It is discovery rather than an exact operative basis or consumer authority.
concepts.label: Version-Line Selector

conditions: The optional carrier is used.
concepts.definition: An optional mutable project-qualified convenience carrier aligned to the selector's latest-published commit.

grounding.quote:
- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

concepts.label: Release Branch

concepts.definition: The release process has three ordered phases: mutable candidate construction; immutable RC publication with monotonic version-line advancement; exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.
concepts.label: Release process

concepts.definition: Qualification is evidence-based evaluation of the exact cut and its claims. Acceptance is the human Product authority's verdict over that immutable subject, distinct from publication, selector advancement and consumer adoption.

grounding.quote:
An RC is accepted only when the required exact-cut review and operator
checks are complete and the human authority accepts that exact subject.

concepts.label: Exact-cut qualification and acceptance

concepts.definition: Consumer adoption is a separate explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs, verifies and pins an immutable RC. Its read-only Adoption Plan binds current definition bytes and basis to the target cut, tag object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, and emits a deterministic digest.

grounding.quote: Presentation and mutation are separate invocations.

concepts.label: Consumer adoption and Adoption Plan

conditions: A surface is carried by the cut.
concepts.definition: Optional release-scoped surfaces include release notes, release and installed-distribution manifests, dependency declarations, package or installed-carrier metadata, qualification receipts, and branch and tag identity declarations.

grounding.quote: An immutable RC cut may carry release-scoped surfaces such as

concepts.label: Release-scoped assets

concepts.definition: The Product release subject is the declared exact Product member set or artifact. Release-scoped claim surfaces describe it; co-located mutable source-project fields can be explicitly excluded from both. The repository commit is their wider carrier, not automatic Product membership.

grounding.quote:
A repository commit carries those declared sets but does not make every
co-located file or sibling Project Subtree a Product member.

concepts.label: Product release subject

conditions: A Product authority explicitly declares the relation because a source corpus and required distributed or derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set.
concepts.definition: A Release-Matched Asset Cohort is an explicitly declared cross-Product set naming every required Product and asset, exact source dependency, owning authorities, qualification boundary and publication transaction. The STDO stack's closed cohort consists of its exact standards cut; distributed spec plugin and host assets; exact Axiom Indexer mechanics Product; exact STDO Representation Product; and released a_c.STDO program and constraint map or equivalent semantic index, with complete source inventory, member digests, member-set digest and derivation cut identity.

grounding.quote: For a release-matched STDO stack, the closed cohort contains all of

concepts.label: Release-Matched Asset Cohort

conditions: A coordinated STDO cohort is being constructed.
concepts.definition: The bounded two-commit construction freezes source STDO in commit A and derived Products and cohort record in commit B. The installed manifest includes the annotated STDO tag object; placing that identity and its derived child bytes in the same commit would be self-referential. Local construction and qualification precede one atomic publication transaction.

grounding.quote:
Exact installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object,
so a same-commit carrier containing both that identity and derived child
bytes would be self-referential.

concepts.label: Two-commit cohort publication

concepts.definition: A successor disposition is a claim about one affecting predecessor claim: conserved means retained; superseded means replaced by an accepted successor relation; intentionally removed means removed by current Product authority; not applicable means no successor effect with a bounded reason. These are predicates to evaluate, not result values. An unresolved disposition states no claim and has no result.

grounding.quote: An unresolved disposition states no claim and so has no result:

concepts.label: Successor semantic disposition

concepts.definition: The source-disposition table records the member's claims that rc.2 RELEASE_METHOD rows are conserved and routed to current loci. Routes are provenance only. Recorded generalisations remove emphasis, replace method-relative references with §9 or this member, use British spelling, and render 'must remain usable' as the declaration condition 'need to remain usable', without a new obligation. Generic release objects are defined in FOUNDATIONS and realised here.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

concepts.label: Release source-disposition record

concepts.definition: SPEC_METHOD is a Tier 2 particular-method member owning method identity and position, constitutional chain and surfaces, manifesto and litmus tests, requirement and design law, trace closure, live-surface law, outcome conservation, change management, consistency and sprint boundaries, ambiguity governance, lifecycle sufficiency, lineage, release-version boundary, migration, procedures, design records and build-tenant binding. It is realised from FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION, not foundational itself. PRODUCT_DEFINITION, ASSURANCE, TICKETS and RELEASE respectively carry project binding, testing law, work carriers and release mechanics.

grounding.quote:
nothing here is foundational, every clause
names the principle that requires it

concepts.label: SPEC_METHOD

concepts.definition: Spec-driven development treats specification as constitutional source to make software re-derivable, auditable and correctable under explicit authority. Its declarative bias recommends primarily declaring truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence surfaces; imperative procedure remains subordinate to declared authority.

grounding.quote:
Its
overriding bias is declarative rather than imperative:

concepts.label: Spec-driven development

concepts.definition: The method is a process constitution and meta-constitutional account of relationships, sufficiency, requirement truth and authority flow. It should bootstrap a new spec-driven process if implementation disappears; together with surviving domain specification it can reconstruct the project. Bound WHAT surfaces retain constitutional authority; design and realisation define HOW. Conventional paths locate roles without constituting mandatory layouts.

grounding.quote: Its role is meta-constitutional:

concepts.label: Process constitution

conditions: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:method-identity under the selected complete basis.
concepts.definition: STDO names four areas: Specification owned by SPEC_METHOD; Ticketing by TICKETS; Design by DESIGN_MODULE; Outcome-Driven Development, including its complete identity and realisation meaning, by ODD. An area is a body of method law, not an independently selectable released member.

grounding.quote:
The expansion does not make the four owning
members independently selectable and does not reduce the released product
to four members:

concepts.label: STDO method identity

concepts.definition: F10 explains how specification governs realisations, under instance premises of owned layers, layered surfaces, several realisations and immutable releases. It distinguishes consequences from owned choices. Cited standing is P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 under non-reacquirability of step-produced facts; P5 derived from P0 and P6 under the open-world premise.

grounding.quote: decides how a product's specification governs its realisations.

concepts.label: Chain, outcome and build-tenant binding family

concepts.definition: The homeostatic chain is Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis → Repricing at the change-class-selected layer. Every link is an owned responsibility. Code, Events and Projection use the selected execution binding's carriers; the chain does not demand a software codebase or event store where the binding selects neither.

grounding.quote:
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
  → Repricing at the layer its change class names

concepts.label: Constitutional chain

concepts.definition: Goals state current overriding concerns for a bounded work wave, more immediate than intent and higher-level than product definition and requirements. They keep temporary focus out of deeper layers until intentionally repriced there.

grounding.quote: The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface:

concepts.label: Goals

concepts.definition: Intent states purpose, direction, why the system exists and which directional changes are in or out of scope. It carries no optional realisation detail unless that detail is itself constitutional.

grounding.quote:
Intent states why the
system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope; it carries
no optional realisation detail unless that detail is itself constitutional.

concepts.label: Intent

concepts.definition: The product-definition surface states the mutable source project's current concrete product, key terms, boundaries and decomposable end-state shape in present-tense terms. It bridges direction to requirements and is neither immutable release cut nor installed product. Its routing role binds actual authority locations and tenant realisations.

grounding.quote:
It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product;

concepts.label: Product Definition

concepts.definition: Requirements are the full constitutional WHAT: invariant truths, capabilities, constraints, governance and verification obligations that the project must make true. They have explicit acceptance criteria and must support downstream design derivation, including material lifecycle obligations or named ambiguity gaps.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state stable obligations
that must be true; they carry explicit acceptance criteria

concepts.label: Requirements

concepts.definition: Design is the structural HOW: decisions, interfaces, carriers, topology, file placement, entry and control surfaces, runtime wiring, packaging and lawful tenant boundaries that realise requirement truth. ADRs are durable design records, not another constitutional layer above design or a second requirement surface.

grounding.quote: Design is the structural how:

concepts.label: Design and ADRs

concepts.definition: Realisation performs design decisions as software, human procedure or both according to the selected execution environment. Events retain what happened in an event stream, ledger, signed record or observation log; Projection reconstructs current truth where that record suffices, without necessarily replaying a complete event stream. Delta reveals divergence from intended truth; Scenarios test operational meaning; Gap analysis exposes constitutional insufficiency; Repricing updates the lawful layer.
concepts.label: Realisation and evidence feedback

concepts.definition: A build tenant's execution binding separates requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment. The source also distinguishes construction steps, data meaning and execution as three accounts. Binding design identifies operations, outcome values mapped into the core, resource measures, units and boundaries, and any mappings between accounts.

grounding.quote: the division of a binding into requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment

concepts.label: Build-tenant binding

concepts.definition: Requirement category and lifecycle status are independent declared-state axes. Categories are Capability (provided behaviour/function/surface), Constraint / Guarantee (invariant or behavioural bound), Governance (lifecycle/authority/visibility/release/operator policy), and Verification (tests/evidence/traceability/qualification/forensics). Statuses are Active, Deferred, Superseded and Orphaned. Category is neither priority nor a user-facing-feature claim.

grounding.quote: Every live requirement family is classified on two independent axes

concepts.label: Requirement classification

conditions: A product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface or capability is material.
concepts.definition: Its operational lifecycle is intent, requirement, build, assurance, release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry and retirement. Each phase has a declared state: answered; not applicable with a reason; or unknown with a named Gap: or Unanswered: marker. These states are not evaluation results.

grounding.quote:
whose canonical chain is intent, requirement, build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry, retirement.

concepts.label: Operational lifecycle

conditions: A work wave bears a product outcome.
concepts.definition: The wave selects one unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome and its acceptance interval. Evidence distinguishes material advance (accepted movement toward that outcome, the only product-progress category), bounded prerequisite readiness naming the enabled obligation, preservation and repeated proof, and regression. Churn and forecast revision retain ACTIVATION §5 meanings.

grounding.quote:
Every product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected,
unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome and declares the
acceptance interval for that instance.

concepts.label: Product-outcome-bearing work wave

grounding.quote: release process is separate from live specification and owns neither Product meaning nor consumer adoption.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Release handling is downstream of intake triage; an open release window authorises no untriaged change. Release operations do not decide live Product meaning or adoption. Refusal, stopping, fail-closed outcomes, invalid states and failed checks report in the one core and none means success; an operation outcome is not acceptance. The family table accounts for §§1–9 and traces FOUNDATIONS §2 without owning it; §10 open questions and §11 dispositions decide nothing. Consumers apply only the owning rule's decisions. P3 and P6 are independent; P0 recovered; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirability of step-produced facts. The ref-binding row also invokes P1 despite not listing it in that row's premise column.
constraints.uncertainty: The core result algebra and full foundation standing law are referenced, not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the
version-line selector may move. An immutable RC tag never moves (P3).

constraints.statement: Equal version text collapses none of the seven release identities. Branches and the version-line selector may move; immutable RC tags never move.

conditions: The shared-source ref requirements apply to every future publication from a shared release source.
exceptions: A single-project source may retain an explicitly declared unqualified profile only while exactly one independently released project exists.
The separate naming rule permits another spelling only under a ref policy proving collision freedom and preserving all identity distinctions.
Historical refs are conserved prospectively rather than renamed.

grounding.quote:
`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the
release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line.

constraints.statement: The explicit Product-authority-assigned namespace matches [a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*, contains no slash, is source-local unique and stable for the continuing line. Directory/display/definition/package names and matching versions neither infer nor reassign it. Shared-source shapes are refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>, refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>, refs/tags/<project>/v<version>, and refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>. Future shared cuts/selectors cannot use unqualified v<version>-rc.<n> or v<version>. Adding a second independently released project requires qualification before either publishes another cut. The allocated Specification Stack namespaces are specification_methodology, axiom_indexer and stdo_representation; their allocation neither merges Products nor implies dependency or composition.

conditions: The immutable cut is in a shared release source.
exceptions: The canonical path '.' alone denotes repository root; there the subtree tree equals the repository-root tree.

grounding.quote: In a shared release source, an immutable cut binds all of

constraints.statement: The cut binds namespace and owning authority; exact qualified ref and annotated tag object; peeled commit and repository-root tree; normalised subtree root at that commit and its exact tree; declared member inventory and release-scoped claim bytes; and required predecessor/successor dispositions. The subtree root is a locator, not Product identity: a slash-separated Git path without leading/trailing slash, empty, '.' or '..' components, except the root notation. Non-root components name exact tree-entry bytes. Moving a project changes locator and cut identity without reassigning namespace. A monorepo tag grants no sibling membership; unrelated sibling bytes remain carrier state. Inventory or payload digest alone, lacking qualified ref, commit, subtree root and tree, is not a complete reacquirable release identity.

conditions: Existing refs or public release coordinates predate project qualification.
The transition rule applies when one version line spans the transition.
exceptions: An additional archival ref may preserve reachability of the same historical tag object.

grounding.quote: Project qualification is prospective.

constraints.statement: Existing unqualified refs retain names, objects, peels and public links; historical tags are not recreated, re-annotated, moved or replaced. Product-local cut names and public logical URIs stay unchanged, including stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/; qualified transport refs are not inserted into that URI. Resolution binds the logical cut to its exact historical or qualified ref and fails closed if a project-local coordinate names different tag objects. Latest is the greatest positive ordinal across that project's preserved historical and qualified future cuts. First qualified publication creates the qualified selector; the old selector stays at its existing object, ceases to be current for the shared source and is not force-moved to imitate qualification.

grounding.quote: There is no second final cut after an accepted RC.

constraints.statement: Publication immediately makes the new highest ordinal discoverable through the selector. Acceptance is a verdict on the exact RC, not a second carrier or final cut. Any changed byte capable of affecting the Product or a release-scoped claim requires publishing and reviewing a higher immutable RC.

conditions: During candidate construction and before RC publication.

grounding.quote:
A material scope change is repriced instead of being silently
absorbed (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Mutable source is explicitly non-operative for released consumers. Before publication the intended Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded source-project state and qualification basis become explicit. Material scope changes require repricing rather than silent absorption.

conditions: Publishing an immutable RC.
Shared-source tag spelling applies in a shared release source.
Atomic push is required by this general procedure where transport supports it; the cohort procedure imposes the stricter atomic-or-refuse rule.
exceptions: The release branch is optional.
A bounded review repair does not alone require a minor-version increment when the intended version line remains applicable.

grounding.quote:
A published RC cut exists to provide one exact subject for review, replay
and possible acceptance.

constraints.statement: Publication requires, in order: confirm triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry; declare exact subject and claims; reconcile release-facing assets; run proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks; commit exact carrier; resolve and record namespace, subtree root and tree; create annotated immutable cut and annotated selector over the same commit; atomically push carrier, RC branch, cut tag, selector and optional release branch where supported; remotely verify tag, selector and used release branch resolve to the highest published RC commit; record enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to reacquire without a mutable checkout. Further work increments n on the still-applicable line. A higher published RC without matching selector advancement is invalid and fail-closed, never authority to resolve the older cut as latest.

exceptions: Artifact presence can establish presence when presence is the exact claim.

grounding.quote: Evidence matches the claim.

constraints.statement: Qualification binds namespace, qualified immutable ref, annotated object, peeled commit, repository tree, subtree root/tree, declared members, exact claim bytes, governing Product/release basis, every claimed property and observation boundary, evidence subjects, owner verdicts, unresolved gaps and complete successor relation to the declared predecessor. Source success proves neither packaged nor installed behaviour; packaging equivalence does not prove semantic behaviour; presence does not prove usability. Acceptance requires completed required exact-cut review and operator checks plus human acceptance of that exact subject. A qualifying-byte change leaves the verdict on the old RC and requires a higher RC; acceptance does not move/rewrite the selector or create a final carrier.

conditions: Advancing a project version line.
exceptions: The release branch is aligned only when used.
The general push step is atomic where the transport supports it.

grounding.quote: Forward movement is strictly monotonic by RC ordinal.

constraints.statement: Identify exact new immutable tag, ordinal and peel; confirm no higher ordinal exists and selector is absent or on a lower ordinal of the same project line; atomically create/force-update the annotated selector to the highest RC commit; align any release branch; atomically push the carrier and complete relevant refs where supported; remotely verify selector peel and matching immutable annotated tag. Refuse absent matching annotated cut tags, an already existing higher ordinal, backward movement, or selector/release-branch misalignment. Later defects require higher immutable RCs, never moving old cut tags or rolling selectors backward. Selector meaning is v<version>-rc.latest; every concrete RC remains addressable.

conditions: Resolving or adopting through a version-line channel.
exceptions: An older cut can be intentionally retained by explicit immutable URI and digest using exact-basis operations such as sync, not through the latest channel.

grounding.quote:
Moving the Git
version-line selector does not update any consumer.

constraints.statement: The channel stdo://channels/<version> may remain discovery, while operative basis is exact stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/ plus installed-manifest digest. Resolution requires an annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; missing peeled-selector ref fails closed and cannot be treated as a lightweight tag. Enumerate published tags in the selected namespace, including preserved historical cuts during transition, choose greatest positive ordinal and require cut and current selector to be annotated tags peeling to the same commit. Selector lag or another target fails closed. Same-line channel adoption below the definition's current exact ordinal is refused. Selector movement itself changes no consumer.

conditions: Mutation of one Product Definition or a fleet is proposed.

grounding.quote:
Planning inside a mutating invocation is not
external presentation and cannot authorise itself.

constraints.statement: Read-only presentation and mutation are separate invocations. Mutation requires the presented deterministic plan digest as operator acceptance and re-derives that exact digest before any definition change. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates acceptance. Fleet adoption uses one aggregate digest over all exact per-definition plans. Planning inside mutation supplies no external presentation or self-authorisation.
constraints.uncertainty: The hashing rule and command boundaries are delegated to unsupplied PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4.

conditions: A release-scoped surface is used.

grounding.quote:
Before RC publication, each used surface is reconciled to the exact RC
subject.

constraints.statement: Reconcile every used release-scoped surface to the exact subject before publication. Any subsequent change to its bytes creates a different candidate requiring a higher RC tag. Selector advancement adds no Product bytes and has no content-reconciliation phase. Exact version/RC identity belongs in release-scoped carriers and consumer basis bindings; live constitutional version-label use follows the specification-surface rule.

conditions: Before qualification and after publication, respectively.

grounding.quote:
Once the immutable RC is published, no post-review
carrier delta is admitted into that cut.

constraints.statement: Before qualification declare namespace and exact subtree root, exact member set/artifact, describing claim surfaces and co-located mutable fields excluded from both. Subtree tree and member inventory distinguish subject from carrier. No post-review carrier delta enters a published cut. Publication-caused tickets or source-work bookkeeping are recorded afterward on the continuing source branch and cannot move the immutable tag.

conditions: A cohort is explicitly declared.
exceptions: An old stale index may remain immutable history, but cannot accompany changed source as the current cohort.

grounding.quote:
Equal versions establish release
matching only.

constraints.statement: Co-location, equal version text and a common actor cannot infer a cohort. Every required member uses exact suffix <version>-rc.<n>; cut names/refs render v<version>-rc.<n>, embedded asset fields omit v. Qualification normalises only this leading marker and requires exact suffix equality. Equality merges neither Product identities, inventories, tags, acceptance judgments nor release authorities. Missing, stale, differently versioned, other-source-cut or non-reproducible source-member/digest-closure members make the cohort incomplete. Any covered source-member change invalidates the old derived successor candidate; regenerate, mechanically validate, independently qualify where required, and release the index under the same new cut name.

conditions: Constructing and publishing a coordinated STDO cohort.
exceptions: Optional release branches are included only when used.

grounding.quote: a mandatory post-tag, pre-push gate re-runs qualification

constraints.statement: Commit A freezes exact STDO corpus, plugin, release record and qualification bytes. Create its annotated cut locally without pushing; install and verify that exact cut to obtain the manifest identity for every derived Product/index. Derive and freeze Axiom Indexer, STDO Representation, semantic index and cohort record in B. Qualify B against the exact local STDO tag before child immutable tags. Prepare annotated child cuts and every Product-local RC branch, selector and used release branch. The mandatory post-tag/pre-push gate requalifies all local annotated objects/peels, selectors, branches, normalised versions, target commits and exact closed ref set, and fetches/binds expected remote object IDs or required absence for every destination. One atomic transaction publishes only that qualified carrier branch and complete Product ref set.

conditions: Publishing or remotely verifying a coordinated cohort.
exceptions: Later bookkeeping may use a later commit without moving immutable cohort tags.

grounding.quote:
If the remote does not support atomic ref publication, publication
refuses.

constraints.statement: No atomic remote support means refusal, with no sequential-push fallback. Immutable cuts are create-only and require bound remote absence. Every mutable carrier/RC/selector/release ref uses an explicit per-ref compare-and-swap lease in that same transaction. A missing expected ref, unexpected existing tag or changed remote object ID stops publication; refetch and repeat complete content and local-ref-graph qualification before another push. Lease mismatch permits no unguarded force, partial push or in-place expectation update. Remote verification fails closed for required refs absent, lightweight, differently versioned, on wrong Product commits, or with selector/release-branch mismatch.

exceptions: Same-version historical backfill is allowed only when separately authorised recovery law names the exception.

grounding.quote:
Post-publication qualification verifies the same relation from remote refs
and refuses a partial cohort

constraints.statement: Content qualification binds A's exact STDO tag/manifest, B's source tree, all Product target refs, version markers, inventories, index bytes and full corpus digest closure, establishing taggability without changed qualifying bytes. After refs exist, local-ref-graph qualification binds objects, peels, commits, exact push set and all remote expectations to that unchanged content result. Post-publication qualification checks the same relation remotely and refuses partial cohorts. Authorised recovered assets still bind exact historical cut and same cut name; remote completeness remains mandatory. Recovery cannot move the historical tag, add subject bytes or pretend the cohort was atomic at original publication. Normal successors use atomic publication. New/changed cohort law governs only a higher immutable RC containing its qualifying bytes and never retroactively coordinates an earlier cut.
constraints.uncertainty: No separately authorised recovery law is supplied.

conditions: An RC is considered for acceptance.
exceptions: Independent exact-cut review is required where applicable.
Release-blocking gaps may instead be addressed by explicitly narrowing the claimed scope.
Retained evidence satisfies gates only under the referenced validity conditions.

grounding.quote: Each criterion is a mandatory gate

constraints.statement: All seven gates apply regardless of selected post-change checks: passed pre-RC qualification of the declared subject; passed independent exact-cut review where required; completed required operator review; stable intended scope and successor relation; accurate release-scoped assets; closure of all release-blocking gaps including EVALUATION §5 promotion blockers, or explicit narrowing; and human Product-authority acceptance of the exact immutable identity. Acceptance neither advances nor rolls back the selector. Adoption separately evaluates the channel's exact latest target and mutates only after its digest-bound plan is accepted.
constraints.uncertainty: External rules determine promotion-blocking findings and retained-evidence validity.

conditions: A release claim depends on an external backend, transport or operator-facing service.

grounding.quote:
A clean skip caused by an unhealthy external dependency is an evaluation
not performed, which has no result

constraints.statement: An external dependency may remain outside Product for carrier/migration classification while still blocking its dependent claim. A clean skip due to unhealthy dependency is Not performed with no result; it may preserve correct classification but establishes no capability pass. Before acceptance, qualify the claim against a healthy dependency or narrow it.

conditions: A successor evolves predecessor semantic claims.
exceptions: Earlier conserved evidence can be reused only where owning text and carrying consumer bindings are unchanged, or a change is shown not to affect the claim.

grounding.quote:
Every
predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor receives one semantic
disposition

constraints.statement: Name an exact immutable predecessor and keep that origin fixed for the candidate. Give each predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor one semantic disposition evaluated on evidence. Unresolved dispositions block affected-claim qualification. Patch absence is not loss if successor-native behaviour preserves the claim; names/code similarity are not conservation evidence. Compare the same material case, scope and authority across owning text and consumer bindings: obligations, permissions, prohibitions, missing triggers/exceptions/premises and decision-changing counterexamples. Indicative wording can bind; replacing must/shall alone proves neither conservation nor supersession. Obligations, preferences, every permitted exception and scope condition must survive for conservation. Package-wide equivalence assertions prove no individual claim. Pre-test conserved records must be reevaluated before qualification and remain unresolved until then.

grounding.quote:
a recorded disposition establishes
nothing until it is evaluated, so no disposition stands as a result

constraints.statement: Qualification evaluates each disposition's stated predicate and records a separate core result. A successor claim disposition differs from an owner's acceptance-result disposition of an assessed candidate. Unresolved disposition is a planned assessment without a closed result and supplies no claim/result. Where maintenance or support lines may affect retained claims, release basis names watched source, observation boundary, inclusion policy and successor candidate; relevant changes receive semantic dispositions at material integration and exact-cut qualification. Consumers own record, branch strategy, comparison and proof mechanism. EVALUATION §5 owns acceptance requirements for the disposition record and applies, rather than belongs to, this section.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced acceptance and core-result laws are not supplied in full.

grounding.quote:
it
decides nothing beyond the rules it names.

constraints.statement: Source-disposition rows assert conservation for release context/position, seven identities, namespace/ref law, subtree identity, historical conservation, phases, candidate construction, publication, qualification, advancement, adoption, naming, assets, cohorts, two-commit publication, recovery, subject/carrier, acceptance, external dependencies, successor conservation and both open questions. They are provenance records, not independently evaluated conservation results. The family table and Results paragraph are new; successor dispositions are newly stated as evaluated claims and unresolved assessments as resultless gaps. grounding.quote: The authoritative split is strict:

constraints.statement: The method defines process constitution; GOALS conventionally locates work concerns, INTENT domain direction, PRODUCT the current mutable-source definition, specification/requirements the derived live requirements, and shared plus tenant-local design the mechanism. Actual locations are bound by the product definition and tenant registry beneath one shared specification. Bound WHAT defines WHAT; no build tenant, design, code, definition overlay or derived surface becomes co-equal constitutional authority. Conventional names require neither relocation nor duplication. Declared requirement structure/family boundaries are preferred to one imperative catch-all; folder placement itself is not constitutional.

exceptions: Hard-stop prerequisite failures are not subject to ordinary discretionary blocking/escalation policy.
constraints.statement: The canonical statement is an owner-routed compression, not an independent rule owner. Every product publishes a layout-neutral definition locating governing constitution, local constitutional decisions, collective reference-frame bases, WHAT, independent tenant HOW, work surfaces and explicit composition; the overlay routes rather than rivals truth. Material terms resolve only within declared context, owner, selected basis and scope; equal spelling grants no shared meaning/authority, seams require explicit import/translation/equivalence/disambiguation, and zero or multiple applicable meanings fail closed. Major boundaries must surface ambiguity and reduce lawful interpretations; detection is mandatory while blocking/escalation follows declared risk policy except hard stops. Implementations do not replace constitutional documents. Scenarios supply end-to-end proof where claims need it. Sprints price proof and force close review, confer no authority and cannot hide drift.
constraints.uncertainty: Several named owners, ambiguity policies and hard-stop predicates are outside this excerpt.

conditions: A tenant binding or mapping between construction accounts is declared.

grounding.quote: the kind of executor alone neither accepts nor rejects a realisation

constraints.statement: Different means may realise the same obligations; obligation fitness, not executor kind, decides conformity. Human execution is not adjudication, convenient stacks weaken nothing, and structural validity does not prove correct execution. Only the obligation owner can weaken it through a WHAT change. Bindings make operations, core-mapped outcomes and resource measures with units/boundaries evaluable by finite actors; a calculus applies wherever its declared laws hold regardless of executor. Tenant design selects calculus/environment and required resource bounds; project law owns multi-tenant development mechanics. Construction steps, semantics and execution remain separate accounts; any mapping states and discharges preservation under ACTIVATION refinement and, when recorded in a_c, AC-013. Which accounts are joined and supporting environmental evidence belong to the tenant binding.
constraints.uncertainty: Full binding rules, core mapping, resource-limit law and transformation preservation law are external references.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: The table accounts for §§1–3, §6 and §§9–11; canonical compression and source dispositions add no decisions, while §8 applies ACTIVATION's step and priority laws. Table choices include chain layers/order and conventional names, categories/statuses and ADR conventions, lifecycle phases/gap markers, selected-outcome policy and evidence kinds, eight-step adoption chain, method identity, scoped should-force and optional design vocabulary, binding decomposition and resource choices. FOUNDATIONS owns lineage and the Product Intent owns the three-account choice. Closure evidence includes authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible and remaining open pressure; closure conditions and evidence law remain with TICKETS, EVALUATION and ASSURANCE. Reusable method changes preserve one authority relation from evidence through to the realising consumer. Consumer applications add no owning decisions; evidence assembly and account mappings have no separate consumer rule.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed choices and consumer loci outside the supplied excerpt remain references, not reconstructed rules.

exceptions: Transitional paths can remain live only if explicitly retained as compatibility features.

grounding.quote:
If these claims do not hold, the
work is not spec-driven.

constraints.statement: Establish work goals before deeper repricing, intent before implementation, and explicit present-tense product definition before detailed requirements. Requirements cover full WHAT; design explicitly bridges requirements and code, which must be derivable from both rather than justified by precedent. Declarative truth/boundaries are preferred to imperative procedure. Major gates reduce interpretation space before downstream work. Claims need scenarios, tests, events, projection and delta evidence. Constitutional gaps require specification change. Authority remains directional through iteration. Live surfaces state current reality; superseded transitional paths are removed unless explicitly retained compatibility. Derived artifacts, indexes, matrices, reports, automation and generated views are read models, never constitutional truth.

conditions: Any listed failure holds.

grounding.quote: The work is not spec-driven if any of these holds

constraints.statement: Work is not spec-driven if a competent team cannot derive intent from goals, product definition from intent, requirements from product, design from requirements, or code from requirements plus design; a live requirement lacks explicit status/category/design owner or downstream realisation/explicit deferment; code lacks requirement/design authority; a live constitutional domain artifact is rewritten in place; a capability lacks operational evidence; triage locates drift in constitutional source without repricing it; major boundary ambiguity is neither recorded nor explicitly governed; or a material product/module/function/application/runtime surface/capability has neither lifecycle signal nor recorded gaps for unanswered release/deployment/live-use/telemetry/retirement questions.

grounding.quote: A failure at any boundary is a specification defect of the upper layer.

constraints.statement: Spec-drivenness requires ordered reconstructability by a competent team: goals to intent, intent to product, product to requirements, requirements to design, requirements/design to code. Sufficiency is not determinism; hiding major ambiguity cannot cross a sufficient boundary. Failure diagnoses the upper surface: goals insufficient to orient work, intent too vague/contradictory, product undecomposable, requirements underspecified/contradictory/polluted by incidental implementation, or design incomplete/ambiguous/inoperational. ADRs/design are load-bearing bridges. Accepted relations are reusable only on exact basis after applicability/invalidation checks. Ambiguity governance and the design profile's coverage, change gate and reuse rules remain applicable.
constraints.uncertainty: The generic sufficiency, reconstruction grants and design-profile gates are not supplied in full.

conditions: Concrete real use-case pressure reveals a constitutional gap, rather than only missing implementation.

grounding.quote:
Ad hoc coding pressure does not generate
intent; explicit gap analysis does.

constraints.statement: Scenarios, deployment or external review can expose what the current constitution cannot express. Explicit gap analysis selects re-entry at the change class's layer, with new goals or intent where work wave, direction or scope changes, then propagation through that class's downstream span. A gap becomes intent only once concrete; repeated real pressure, not abstract speculation or ad hoc coding, generates it. Implementation, testing, replay and scenario gaps feed cumulative repricing; requirements/design refine and code is repeatedly re-derived while authority direction remains fixed.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete change-class mapping is not supplied.

conditions: A downstream specification artifact is to be treated as complete.

grounding.quote:
Before a downstream specification artifact is treated as complete, the
whole affected span is checked:

constraints.statement: Goals do not substitute for requirements and Product is not release notes. Product states intended use, release/install, live use, observability and retirement/supersession posture where material. Requirements have acceptance criteria, derivability and material lifecycle obligations or named gaps. Design remains downstream; ADRs are not requirements. Live constitutional law uses present tense; obsolete law is deleted, superseded or moved to commentary, never retained merely for historical comfort or migration. Version branding cannot merely signal recency. Before completeness, check the whole affected span for clear change class, lawful re-entry, downstream derivability and agreement among active intent, product, requirements, design and qualification in scope. Failure leaves the gate open.

conditions: An upstream constitutional surface does not already constrain the realisation choice.
exceptions: Paths, filenames and packaging may belong to requirements when constitutionally necessary.

grounding.quote: choosing it is part of design, not a separate upstream authority

constraints.statement: Requirements state required control/delivery surfaces; design chooses their mechanism. Unconstrained stack, carrier, runtime, human process or combination is a design-declared execution binding. Agent-facing bootstrap/control requirements can require presence, bare axioms and routing to canonical method; design chooses entry documents, embedded blocks, compiled artifacts or other lawful topology. Hardcoding placement/filenames without constitutional necessity absorbs design into requirements and impairs re-derivation.

exceptions: No particular language, elimination of all imperative code, monadic/category-theory vocabulary, or universal custom-algebraic replacement for exceptions is required.

grounding.quote: The vocabulary is optional; the law is not.

constraints.statement: Semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth and effects should be explicit at the edge. Needing orchestration code, mutable state, service methods or fallback defaults to determine meaning indicates excessive imperative coupling. Readability, modularity and honesty about meaning/effects are required. Where higher-order or effectful computation composes, an explicit composition/effect algebra is required with applicable identity, closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws. The core should-force remains a recommendation; the explicit algebra and readability obligations retain their required force.
constraints.uncertainty: Profile adoption and full composition laws are external.

exceptions: Concrete realisation detail belongs upstream only when itself constitutional.

grounding.quote:
A live requirement
is incomplete if either axis is missing.

constraints.statement: Every live family has explicit header Status and Category; neither axis may be absent and nothing live remains unclassified. Deferred retains an honestly recorded not-yet-operative/realised obligation without claiming closure; Superseded requires Implements and Supersedes in the governing design record; Active requires an owning design decision; Orphaned is removed or explicitly superseded. All categories remain constitutional, not necessarily marketed features; requirements should avoid prematurely freezing realisation. Statuses, categories, legacy classes, evidence kinds, migration old-path/inherited-material/implementation classes, ADR statuses and change classes are declared states, map to no core value and cannot substitute for evaluated predicates/results. Active/material advance is not satisfied; Deferred/Orphaned is not falsified. Successor work still needs separate RELEASE dispositions: Active can be semantically superseded, Superseded supplies no accepted successor relation, and Orphaned supplies no authorised removal.

exceptions: A live requirement may have explicit honest deferment instead of realised downstream closure.

grounding.quote:
No hidden product
surface is allowed;

constraints.statement: Every live requirement family maps to one or more owning design decisions; every ADR/design record explicitly grounds itself through Implements:. Every live requirement closes through design, code and tests or honest deferment. Shipping code and tests trace to live requirements and authorising design; working behaviour without trace is accidental law. Unowned requirements, ungrounded design, unrecorded deferment and ownerless code are drift. Tests preserving implementation habit lock in drift. Persistent event/projection delta requires triage distinguishing code, requirement/design stack, predictive model and observation causes. A capability with requirements/design but no scenario has unverified operational meaning. Feature treatment of guarantee/governance/verification is misclassification; in-place correction corrupts constitutional history. Unexpressible real-use gaps re-enter Requirements or upstream according to change class, not through a code hack.

Live domain artifacts, once published as live
constitutional surfaces, are immutable in place;

constraints.statement: Live surfaces are versioned constitutional history, not scratch space. Wrong live artifacts are superseded by a new version or withdrawn/deleted from the live surface, never silently mutated in place. Superseded transitional paths, migration scaffolds and fallbacks retire and gain no permanent authority. History remains in version control, operational events where present and superseded artifacts. Compatibility shims need not ship forever.

grounding.quote: Silent absence is not a valid lifecycle answer.

constraints.statement: Product and requirements provide enough constitutional signal to derive intended lifecycle or explicitly record ambiguity; they need not prescribe every phase's mechanism or make every requirement a release plan. Product names boundary, use, release/install, live-use, observability and retirement/supersession posture where material. Requirements state invariant lifecycle, ownership, source-truth, authority and interpretation obligations. Each phase is answered, reasoned not-applicable or a named gap. Missing signal cannot be invented through local convention, implementation precedent, prompts or fixtures: reprice the owning surface or retain explicit governed debt. Phase states map to no result; an evaluation supplies its own predicate/core value, and answered/not-applicable is not satisfied.

grounding.quote:
The exact bound outcome instance stops selecting later product-progress
work when the owning authority accepts it;

constraints.statement: Progress and supported-path promotion are evaluated against the same selected outcome; only accepted material advance projects product progress. After acceptance, witnesses remain preservation/regression evidence; further work is preservation, a bounded prerequisite for another admitted outcome, or a lawfully repriced change, never additional progress on the accepted instance. Choosing another already-defined unresolved outcome is goals/work sequencing; changing meaning/scope or adding an outcome requires Product re-entry. Completed matrices, ledgers, inventories, design artifacts, suites or other evidence cannot select, enlarge or replace the outcome; even product assurance evidence does not author the claim.

conditions: Material realisation growth within a product-outcome-bearing wave.
exceptions: Independent parallel work may proceed under its own admitted basis without counting as the governed outcome's progress.

grounding.quote:
Ended authority cannot be renewed by repair,
continuation, evidence, active ticket or run state, or prior admission;

constraints.statement: Growth requires selected unresolved outcome, admitted named bounded prerequisite, or admitted named bounded experiment whose observation discriminates a stated decision for it. Prerequisites/experiments authorise only their provisional bounds: no enlarged outcome, downstream authority, promotion, closure or waiver of applicable design/safety/authority/release law. Admission/renewal belongs to wave owner or bounded proxy and is durably recorded in goals/tickets with bounds and exhaustion/falsification conditions. Ticket/contract drafting or validation, active status and prior admission create/extend/renew nothing. Acceptance, prerequisite discharge, experiment observation/decision resolution, admitted terminal condition, rejection, withdrawal, supersession, repricing-away or falsification ends the basis. More material work needs new admission. Retention grants no growth; consumer-owned salvage carries only explicitly re-adopted semantics, not enclosing authority, dependencies, completion or work-selection power. Regression/unresolved gaps block only affected-path promotion. Outcome success is necessary delivery evidence, not complete Product/release closure.
